claims.sourceText: Report of Inspection of MKULTRA, memorandum for the Director of Central Intelligence, 26 July 1963, National Security Archive John Marks Collection Box 8, https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/sites/default/files/documents/1963-07-26%20JM%20Box%208%20F2%20MKUltra-IG_Report-ocr.pdf
claims.text: The Inspector General's 1963 survey states the programme's purpose: 'The MKULTRA activity is concerned with the research and development of chemical, biological and radiological materials capable of employment in clandestine operations to control human behavior.' It records that 'MKULTRA was authorized by the then Director of Central Intelligence, Mr. Allen W. Dulles, in 1953' and that 'Normal procedures for project approval, funding, and accounting were waived.'

claims.sourceText: Report of Inspection of MKULTRA, CIA Inspector General, 26 July 1963, https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/sites/default/files/documents/1963-07-26%20JM%20Box%208%20F2%20MKUltra-IG_Report-ocr.pdf
claims.text: The Agency's own Inspector General placed him one rung below the top of TSD in 1963: 'The present Deputy Chief of TSD, Dr. Sidney Gottlieb, in his then capacity of scientific advisor to the Deputy Director/Plans (DD/P), released a study ... on 21 April 1960, covering his six-month investigation of "Scientific and Technical Problems in Covert Action Operations".'

edges.label: CIA umbrella project, authorized 1953
edges.note: The 1963 Inspector General survey states the programme was authorized by the Director of Central Intelligence in 1953 and run out of the Technical Services Division on a waived-procedure share of its research budget.
